what_it_does: This paper presents a new way to digitally capture analog signals (an ADC—analog-to-digital converter) that achieves very high precision (120dB signal-to-noise ratio, meaning it captures signals 1 million times cleaner than background noise). The key innovation is eliminating idle power drain by using transient comparators (circuits that only consume power when actively comparing) and dynamically generating reference voltages on demand. Unlike prior designs that required a residue amplifier to refine signals or complex calibration circuits, this architecture integrates noise shaping directly into the SAR (successive approximation register) sampling process, similar to how a ZIP file compresses data without destroying it.
